title: Learner 01 | Day 086: Provider adapters and explicit outcomes
body:
## Goal

Implement a generate-draft interface with fake and one real-provider adapter; select model through configuration.

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/core/values/generation.py`

**Method/unit:** `validate_draft_provider`

**Why here:** This is a value boundary: it defines accepted values and rejects invalid local data. It must not import HTTP, storage, or model SDK code.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Fake works offline; unavailable provider produces unavailable status; secrets never enter source control.

**Boundaries:** Keep value checks local; no transport/storage/model calls.

## Research hints

1. Research **Provider adapters and explicit outcomes**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:huggingface.co/docs Provider adapters and explicit outcomes`; use [Hugging Face LLM course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** Why should source text be separated from trusted instructions?

**Review with @YogeshPatil991:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
